gloss: come to rest, settle; be at rest; give rest, set down, leave; rest, resting place; soothing
summary: To come down and stay: the ark settling on the mountains of Ararat, locusts on Egypt, the spirit on the seventy elders (Gen 8:4; Exo 10:14; Num 11:25); and so to be at rest from labour, trouble or enemies, as Yahweh rested on the seventh day (Exo 20:11; Est 9:22). The hiphil gives rest, above all the land with every enemy subdued (Deu 12:10; Jos 21:44), or sets a thing down and leaves it there (Gen 2:15; Exo 16:33). מְנוּחָה and מָנוֹחַ are rest and the place of it, from a camp-site and a wife’s home to the land and Zion, which Yahweh calls “my rest for ever” (Num 10:33; Rut 1:9; Deu 12:9; Psa 132:14); נִיחֹחַ is the “soothing” scent of an offering (Gen 8:21; Lev 23:18). Akkadian nâḫu, Ugaritic nḫ and Arabic anāḫa, “make a camel kneel”, share the sense.

words.gloss: come to rest, settle; be at rest; (hiphil) give rest, set down, leave

stems.gloss: come to rest, settle; rest upon; be at rest

senses.definition: Of something moving, to come down on a place and stay there: the ark on a mountain, a swarm on a land, the priests’ feet in the river, an army on a country.

evidence.note: “The ark rested (וַתָּנַח) … on the mountains of Ararat”, after floating on the waters.
The locusts went up over Egypt “and settled in all its borders”.
“And when it rested (וּבְנֻחֹה)” the ark, which had set out before the camp (Num 10:33–35), halted; Moses then said “Return, Yahweh”.
When the soles of the priests’ feet rest in the waters of the Jordan.
“We will light on him as the dew falls on the ground.”
Rizpah let no bird rest on the bodies by day.
“Aram has settled on Ephraim”: encamped there.
Flies and bees come and settle in the valleys and clefts.

senses.definition: Of the spirit, a hand, a rod, or wisdom and anger, to come upon a person or place and remain there.

evidence.note: “When the spirit rested (כְּנוֹחַ) on them, they prophesied.”
The spirit rested on Eldad and Medad in the camp.
“The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha.”
“The spirit of Yahweh shall rest on him”, the shoot from the stump of Jesse.
The hand of Yahweh will rest on this mountain.
The rod of wickedness shall not rest on the lot of the righteous.
Wisdom rests in the heart of the understanding.
Anger rests in the bosom of fools.

senses.gloss: be at rest, have rest; cease
senses.definition: To be still after labour or trouble: to rest from work on the seventh day, from enemies after a war, or from troubling; set beside “be quiet” and against trouble.

evidence.note: “In six days Yahweh made the heavens and the earth … and rested (וַיָּנַח) on the seventh day.”
“On the seventh day you shall cease, so that your ox and your donkey may rest.”
That your servants may rest as well as you.
“The whole earth is at rest, it is quiet (שָׁקְטָה)”, once the oppressor has ceased.
“I am not at ease, nor quiet, nor at rest (נָחְתִּי), and trouble (רֹגֶז) comes.”
The Jews “rested from their enemies”.
“The days on which the Jews rested from their enemies.”
“When they had rest, they did evil again.”
That I may rest in the day of trouble.
Even in Kittim Sidon will have no rest.
David’s young men spoke to Nabal “and ceased”: waited for his answer.

senses.definition: Of the dead, to be at rest in the grave from labour and trouble, until they rise.

evidence.note: Had he died at birth, “I would have slept; then I would have had rest.”
In the grave “the wicked cease from troubling, and there the weary are at rest.”
The righteous man “enters peace; they rest on their beds”.
The man who strays from understanding will rest in the assembly of the dead (רְפָאִים).
“You shall rest, and stand in your lot at the end of the days.”

stems.gloss: give rest; make rest upon; set down, deposit; leave; let alone, permit

senses.definition: To bring someone to rest: above all, Yahweh’s giving Israel rest from all their enemies round about in the land, and rest to the weary.

evidence.note: “He will give you rest from all your enemies round about, and you will dwell in safety.”
“Yahweh gave them rest round about … not a man of all their enemies stood before them.”
“My presence shall go, and I will give you rest.”
“This is the rest (הַמְּנוּחָה): give rest (הָנִיחוּ) to the weary.”
When Yahweh had given David rest from all his enemies round about.
Solomon: “Yahweh my God has given me rest on every side.”
“I will give him rest from all his enemies round about.”
Yahweh gives rest from sorrow, trouble and hard bondage.
“The spirit of Yahweh gave them rest”, as cattle going down into the valley.
Correct your son and he will give you rest.

senses.definition: To bring something to rest on a person or place: Yahweh’s fury spent on the guilty until it is quieted, his spirit, a blessing, the strokes of his rod.

evidence.note: “My anger shall be accomplished, and I will make my fury rest (וַהֲנִחוֹתִי) on them, and I will be comforted.”
“I will make my fury rest, and my jealousy shall depart from you, and I will be quiet.”
“Those going to the north country have made my spirit rest in the north country.”
To make a blessing rest on your house.
Every stroke of the appointed rod which Yahweh lays on him.
Calmness lays to rest great offences.

senses.definition: To put a thing or person in a place and leave it there: the man in the garden, the manna and the rods before the testimony, stones, offerings, a people on its own land.

evidence.note: Yahweh God took the man “and put him (וַיַּנִּחֵהוּ) in the garden of Eden”.
“Lay it up before Yahweh, to be kept”: the pot of manna.
The rods laid up in the tent of meeting before the testimony.
The high priest leaves the linen garments there.
The priest sets the basket of firstfruits down before the altar.
“Lay them on this rock.”
Samuel wrote the manner of the kingdom in a book and laid it up before Yahweh.
They set the idol in its place, and it stands; it cannot move.
Yahweh will choose Israel again “and set them in their own land”.
“I will put my spirit in you and you shall live, and I will set you in your own land.”
They put the blasphemer in custody.
The ashes of the heifer laid up outside the camp.
Chariots stationed in the chariot cities.
Those who cast righteousness down to the earth.

senses.definition: To let a thing stay where it is, or leave it behind for others.

evidence.note: “They laid it up until the morning, as Moses commanded, and it did not stink.”
He shall not leave any of it until morning.
“Leave one of your brothers with me.”
Yahweh left the nations, not driving them out quickly.
The concubines David left to keep the house.
Elijah left his servant at Beersheba.
They leave their abundance to their children.
Leave it to the man who will be after me.
The nation that serves Babylon will be let remain in its own land.
“You shall leave your name for a curse to my chosen.”
He will again leave them in the wilderness.
Lay up the tithe of the third year within your gates.

senses.definition: To leave someone to themselves, refrain from interfering; and so to let, permit.

evidence.note: “Now let me alone (הַנִּיחָה לִּי), that my anger may burn against them.”
“Let him alone, and let him curse.”
“Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone.”
“He permitted no man to oppress them.”
The rich man’s abundance will not let him sleep.
“Let me feel the pillars.”
It is not for the king’s profit to let them be.
“Do not leave us.”
“Do not leave me to my oppressors.”
In the evening do not withhold (let rest) your hand.
When Moses let his hand rest (let it down), Amalek prevailed.

stems.gloss: be given rest; be set down; (participle) space left

senses.gloss: be given rest; be set down
senses.definition: Passive of the hiphil: rest given, or a thing set in its place; the participle מֻנָּח is the space left open around Ezekiel’s side chambers.

evidence.note: “We are weary, and no rest is given (הוּנַח) us.”
The woman in the ephah “shall be set down (וְהֻנִּיחָה) there on her base” in Shinar.
“That which was left” between the side chambers and the wall.

evidence.locator: Exo.20.11, וַיָּנַח → κατέπαυσεν; Jos.21.44 the same; Exo.33.14, וַהֲנִחֹתִי → καταπαύσω; καταπαύω renders נוּחַ ×10

evidence.note: “If Joshua had given them rest (κατέπαυσεν), he would not afterward have spoken of another day”: of the rest Yahweh gave by Joshua (Jos 21:44; 23:1).
God “rested (κατέπαυσεν) on the seventh day from all his works”, as Exo 20:11 says with נוּחַ.

evidence.locator: Isa.11.2, וְנָחָה → ἀναπαύσεται; Est.9.16, וְנוֹחַ → ἀνεπαύσαντο; 1Ch.22.9 הֲנִחוֹתִי → ἀναπαύσω; ἀναπαύω renders נוּחַ ×19

evidence.note: “The spirit of glory and of God rests (ἀναπαύεται) upon you”, the Septuagint’s word for Isa 11:2.

parallels.note: Be quiet, undisturbed: set beside resting.
Cease: the seventh day’s ceasing and resting together.

opposites.note: Trouble, turmoil: what rest is free of.

phrases.gloss: give rest from all one’s enemies round about
make one’s fury rest on: spend it until it is quieted

senses.definition: Being at rest: relief from weariness, toil and enemies; a settled life.

evidence.note: “A man of rest (אִישׁ מְנוּחָה): I will give him rest from all his enemies round about … peace and quietness.”
“This is the rest: give rest to the weary; and this is the refreshing (מַרְגֵּעָה).”
“I am weary with my groaning, and I find no rest.”
“That you may find rest, each in the house of her husband”: a settled home.
“Blessed be Yahweh, who has given rest to his people Israel.”
Issachar saw that rest was good, and bowed his shoulder to bear.
“He leads me beside waters of rest (מֵי מְנֻחוֹת).”
“Return to your rest, my soul.”
Quiet resting places, beside a peaceful habitation and secure dwellings.
“The word of my lord the king shall be for rest”: a settled end to the matter.
They trod Benjamin down “with ease”, or “at Menuhah”: the sense is uncertain.
Seraiah was שַׂר מְנוּחָה, officer of the resting place (the halting of the march).

senses.gloss: resting place; the land, Yahweh’s dwelling
senses.definition: A place to stop and stay: the camp-site the ark sought out, the land Yahweh gave Israel as inheritance, and Zion, where Yahweh rests among his people.

evidence.note: The ark went before them three days’ journey “to seek out a resting place for them”.
“You have not yet come to the rest and to the inheritance (הַנַּחֲלָה) which Yahweh your God is giving you.”
“I swore in my anger that they shall not enter into my rest”: the generation that died in the wilderness.
“Arise and go, for this is not the rest, because of uncleanness.”
“Arise, Yahweh, to your rest, you and the ark of your strength.”
Zion: “This is my rest for ever; here I will dwell.”
“A house of rest for the ark of the covenant of Yahweh, and for the footstool of our God.”
“Where is the house you will build for me, and where is the place of my rest?”
To the root of Jesse the nations shall seek, “and his resting place shall be glory”.
The burden of Yahweh’s word, and Damascus its resting place.
Stephen quotes Isa 66:1: “what is the place of my rest (καταπαύσεως)?”
Hebrews quotes Psa 95:11.

evidence.locator: Psa.95.11, מְנוּחָתִי → κατάπαυσίν; Deu.12.9 and Isa.66.1 the same; κατάπαυσις renders מְנוּחָה ×4

evidence.note: “They shall not enter into my rest (κατάπαυσιν)”, quoting Psa 95:11.
A promise remains of entering into his rest.
“We who have believed do enter into the rest.”
“What is the place of my rest?”, quoting Isa 66:1.

evidence.locator: Num.10.33, מְנוּחָה → ἀνάπαυσιν; Rut.1.9 the same; 1Ch.22.9 → ἀναπαύσεως; ἀνάπαυσις renders מְנוּחָה ×7

parallels.note: The inheritance: the rest is the land held as inheritance.
Peace and quietness in the days of the man of rest.

phrases.gloss: a house of rest (for the ark)

words.gloss: soothing, a quieting (of an offering’s scent)
words.summary: Found only in רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ, “a scent of soothing”: the smoke of an offering that brings Yahweh’s dealings to rest in acceptance. It names what an offering does, not its smell; the hiphil of the same root is used of Yahweh’s fury brought to rest (Ezk 5:13; 16:42).

senses.definition: That which quiets and satisfies: said of the scent of an offering Yahweh accepts, and withheld from a people he rejects.

evidence.note: “Yahweh smelled the scent of soothing (הַנִּיחֹחַ), and Yahweh said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground.”
Against a rebellious people: “I will not smell the scent of your soothing.”
“With a scent of soothing I will accept you”: the regathered people themselves.
The burnt offering, “a fire offering, a scent of soothing to Yahweh”.
Even with the sin offering, “and the priest shall make a covering for him, and it shall be forgiven him”.
The burnt offering with the sheaf of the עֹמֶר.
The burnt offerings of the fiftieth day.
“My offering, my bread … a scent of my soothing.”

senses.definition: The same offerings made to idols on every high hill, which Yahweh counts as his gifts misused.

evidence.locator: Gen.8.21, נִיחֹחַ → εὐωδίας (ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας for רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ); Lev.23.18 and Ezk.20.41 the same; εὐωδία renders נִיחֹחַ ×41

evidence.note: Christ “gave himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a scent of sweet smell (ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας)”.
The Philippians’ gift: “a scent of sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, well-pleasing to God”.
“We are to God a sweet smell (εὐωδία) of Christ.”

parallels.note: The fire offering, set beside it in the formula.

words.summary: A place to settle, or the settling itself. The tokens counted under it share their spelling with the name Manoah, so its count is inflated; its own uses are six or seven.

senses.gloss: resting place, a place to settle
senses.definition: A place where a creature or person can stop and stay: the dove’s foothold, a home for a widow, a place among the nations.

evidence.note: “The dove found no resting place for the sole of her foot, and returned to him into the ark.”
Among the nations “there shall be no rest for the sole of your foot”.
Judah has gone into exile, dwells among the nations and finds no rest.
“My daughter, shall I not seek rest for you, that it may be well with you?”: a home with a husband.
The night creature finds a resting place in desolate Edom.
David set singers over the house of Yahweh “after the ark had rest (מִמְּנוֹחַ הָאָרוֹן)”.

evidence.locator: Gen.8.9, מָנוֹחַ → ἀνάπαυσιν; ἀνάπαυσις renders מָנוֹחַ ×3

words.summary: Quietness, the calm of the one who is at rest. Three uses (Isa 30:30; Job 17:16; 36:16) are of a coming or setting down, which may belong to this root’s hiphil “set down” or to the separate root נחת “go down”; their link to נוח is not clear. The count includes the name Nahath, which shares the spelling.

senses.definition: Calm and rest, set against toil and raging, and beside quietness and trust.

evidence.note: “In returning and rest (וָנַחַת) you shall be saved; in quietness (הַשְׁקֵט) and in trust shall be your strength.”
“Better a handful with quietness than two handfuls with toil and striving after wind.”
The words of the wise heard in quiet, more than the cry of a ruler among fools.
The stillborn has more rest than the man who never had enough.
With a fool the wise man finds no rest: he rages or laughs.

senses.gloss: a coming down; what is set down (uncertain)
senses.definition: The lighting down of Yahweh’s arm, or what is set on a table: uses whose root is uncertain.

evidence.note: “The lighting down (נַחַת) of his arm”, two verses before “every stroke … which Yahweh lays (יָנִיחַ) on him” (Isa 30:32).
“That which is set on (נַחַת) your table is full of fatness.”
“Will they go down to the bars of the grave, when we descend (or rest) together in the dust?”

evidence.locator: Ecc.4.6, נַחַת → ἀναπαύσεως; ἀνάπαυσις renders נַחַת ×3

words.summary: Once, in Solomon’s prayer, where Psa 132:8 has מְנוּחָה; the corpus counts its one token under מְנוּחָה.

senses.definition: The place where Yahweh and the ark come to rest: the temple.

evidence.note: “Arise, Yahweh God, to your resting place (לְנוּחֶךָ), you and the ark of your strength.”
The same words with לִמְנוּחָתֶךָ.

words.summary: Once, of the king’s release for the provinces at Esther’s feast: a rest granted, whether a holiday or a remission. It is the hiphil “give rest” made a noun.

senses.definition: Rest granted by a ruler to his subjects.

evidence.note: The king made a great feast “and made a release (הֲנָחָה) for the provinces, and gave gifts”.

senses.gloss: cease, be calm; be more bearable
senses.definition: Of wind and waves, to cease; of a judgement, to be lighter, easier to bear.

It will be more bearable (Greek ἀνεκτότερον) for Sodom in the day of judgement.

senses.definition: To give rest to the weary and refresh the spirit.

evidence.note: “Come to me, all you who labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest (אַנִיחְכוּן).”
“If Joshua had given them rest (אַנִיח)”.
They refreshed my spirit and yours.
Onesiphorus often refreshed me.

senses.definition: To set down and leave a thing, as one puts off a garment: of the old way of life.

evidence.note: “Put off (אַנִיחוּ) the old man.”
Put away lying.
Put off anger, wrath, malice.
Let us put off the works of darkness.
Laying aside all malice.

senses.definition: To let others be, put up with them.

evidence.note: “You gladly bear with fools, being wise.”

senses.definition: To rest from labour, take one’s ease, be refreshed; of God on the seventh day, and of the dead.

evidence.note: “God rested (אֶתְנִיח) on the seventh day from all his works.”
He who has entered his rest has rested from his works, as God from his.
“Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord … that they may rest from their labours.”
They were told to rest yet a little while.
“Come apart into a desert place and rest a while.”
“Soul, you have much goods laid up; take your ease.”

senses.definition: Of peace or the spirit, to come upon a person and stay.

evidence.note: “The spirit of glory and of God rests on you.”
“If a son of peace is there, your peace shall rest on him.”

“Our flesh had no rest, but we were troubled on every side.”

That we may lead a quiet and peaceable life.

doctrine.statement: Yahweh promised Israel “the rest and the inheritance” across the Jordan, where he would “give you rest from all your enemies round about” (Deu 12:9–10). Joshua’s generation received it: “Yahweh gave them rest round about … not one word failed” (Jos 21:44–45; 23:1), and Solomon blessed Yahweh “who has given rest to his people Israel” (1Ki 8:56). Yet the generation that came out of Egypt did not enter (“I swore in my anger, they shall not enter into my rest”, Psa 95:11), and Micah told the covetous of his day, “this is not the rest” (Mic 2:10). Hebrews reasons from Psalm 95: “if Joshua had given them rest, he would not afterward have spoken of another day; there remains therefore a keeping of sabbath for the people of God”, and “we who have believed do enter into the rest” (Heb 4:3, 8–9, 11). Yahweh calls Zion “my rest for ever; here I will dwell” (Psa 132:13–14), and of the root of Jesse, to whom the nations will seek, “his resting place shall be glory” (Isa 11:10). From the verses: the rest is the land held as inheritance with every enemy subdued and Yahweh dwelling in Zion; Joshua and Solomon gave a foretaste of it; it remains to be entered when the son of David reigns, and believers enter it now by faith in the promise.

The fourth word grounds Israel’s week on Yahweh’s own: “in six days Yahweh made the heavens and the earth, the sea and all that is in them, and rested (וַיָּנַח) on the seventh day” (Exo 20:11). Israel’s six working days and the seventh day of rest are counted as Yahweh’s were, so the days of creation are days of the same kind. The rest was given to the weakest too: “that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the son of your handmaid and the stranger be refreshed” (Exo 23:12), “that your servant may rest as well as you; and remember that you were a slave in Egypt” (Deu 5:14–15). Hebrews takes the seventh day’s rest as the pattern of the rest still to be entered (Heb 4:4, 9–10).

When Yahweh took of the spirit that was on Moses and put it on the seventy elders, “when the spirit rested on them, they prophesied” (Num 11:25–26); the sons of the prophets saw that “the spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha” when he divided the Jordan as Elijah had (2Ki 2:14–15). Of the shoot from the stump of Jesse it is promised that “the spirit of Yahweh shall rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, of counsel and might, of knowledge and of the fear of Yahweh” (Isa 11:1–2); John saw the spirit descend and remain on Jesus (Joh 1:32–33), to whom God gives the spirit not by measure (Joh 3:34). Peter tells believers who suffer for Christ’s name that “the spirit of glory and of God rests on you” (1Pe 4:14), in the Septuagint’s word for Isa 11:2. From the verses: the spirit is Yahweh’s power coming upon men and remaining on them to fit them for his work; it rested on the prophets in part, on the son of Jesse in full, and on his suffering brethren as the mark of his glory.

Job, wishing he had died at birth, says “I would have slept; then I would have had rest”, for in the grave “the wicked cease from troubling, and there the weary are at rest”, the small and great alike (Job 3:13, 17–19). The righteous man “enters into peace; they rest on their beds” (Isa 57:1–2); the one who strays from understanding “shall rest in the assembly of the dead” (Pro 21:16). Daniel, after hearing that “many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake” (Dan 12:2), is told “you shall rest, and stand in your lot at the end of the days” (Dan 12:13). The Peshitta and the Greek of Revelation use the same word of the faithful dead, who “rest from their labours” (Rev 14:13). From the verses: death is a rest from labour and trouble, a sleep in the dust shared by righteous and wicked, not a conscious life elsewhere; the righteous rest there until they stand up at the end of the days.

After the flood had destroyed all flesh, Noah offered burnt offerings, and “Yahweh smelled the scent of soothing (נִיחֹחַ), and said in his heart, I will not again curse the ground for man’s sake” (Gen 8:20–21). The law names every whole burnt offering, the grain, peace and sin offerings, and the offerings of Lev 23’s feasts, “a scent of soothing to Yahweh” (Lev 1:9; 2:9; 3:5; 4:31; 23:13, 18). But to a people walking contrary to him Yahweh says “I will not smell the scent of your soothing” (Lev 26:31), and when he regathers Israel, “with a scent of soothing I will accept you” (Ezk 20:41): it is the people, not the smoke, that he accepts. Paul says Christ “gave himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a scent of sweet smell” (Eph 5:2), the Septuagint’s rendering of רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ, and calls the Philippians’ gift “a scent of sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, well-pleasing to God” (Php 4:18). From the verses: an offering brought rest because it was the offerer’s life given to God; Christ’s self-offering was that in full, and believers’ own living sacrifices follow it.
